Latest Updates

Chip News & Trends

Industry moves, new flavors, and crunchy innovations from around the globe.

Industry

Gårdschips to Rename Parmesan Chips After EU Name Objection

Hallandsposten reports that Laholm’s environment unit has drafted a decision banning the Gårdschips names Parmesan and Dill och parmesan from 1 May 2027. Environment chief Annica Hegefeldt said grinding, freezing and adding anti-caking agents change the cheese enough that it cannot be called parmesan. SNX Production AB will rename its best-selling flavour and keep the recipe. An Italian producer group cited Parmigiano Reggiano about two years ago. The maker has five months to change the packaging.

🇸🇪 Chips in Sweden →Why chips can’t be called parmesan →
21 Nov 2026Hallandsposten ↗
Industry

Calbee’s Half-Year Profit Climbs as Kataage and Pizza Potato Lift Chip Sales

Calbee grew first-half sales 6% to ¥175.7 billion and operating profit 16.3% for the six months to September 30. Japanese potato-chip sales rose 3% before rebates, led by Kataage Potato and Pizza Potato, while Jagarico recovered after last year’s potato-quality problems cleared. Overseas sales jumped 15.3%, though higher costs squeezed profit there, and full-year forecasts were left unchanged.

🇯🇵 Chips in Japan →
10 Nov 2026Potato Business ↗
Industry

Core Home Buys Tochi, the Salmon-Chip and Asian-Flavor Popcorn Brand

New York consumer-goods group Core Home has acquired Tochi Snacks, a family-founded brand making Norwegian-salmon chips in flavors like Salted Egg, Sriracha and Korean BBQ, plus Asian-inspired gourmet popcorn. The deal closed in October. Tochi, sold through more than 200 wholesale accounts, stays a separate brand while Core Home adds retail reach as part of its push into food and drink.

🇺🇸 Chips in the United States →
10 Nov 2026PR Newswire (Core Home) ↗
New Flavor

Koikeya Opens Orders for Hokkaido Smoked-Salmon Potato Chips

Koikeya has started taking online orders in Japan for a seasonal smoked-salmon chip made with Hokkaido salmon and Japanese potatoes, shipped within three days of frying. A box of six 75 g bags costs ¥1,680 plus delivery, and a 12-bag tasting set adds the salted version for ¥3,192. Orders close at 5 pm Japan time on November 17, via Koikeya’s own shop only.

🇯🇵 Chips in Japan →
9 Nov 2026Grocery Trade News ↗
Industry

PepsiCo to Cut About 1,000 North American Jobs as Snack Volumes Stall

PepsiCo, owner of Lay’s and Doritos maker Frito-Lay, is cutting roughly 1,000 jobs across North America over the coming week to streamline its operations there. The move follows a lowered 2026 earnings outlook in October, after North American food volume came in flat and beverage volume fell 2% in the third quarter despite earlier price cuts and extra marketing.

🇺🇸 Chips in the United States →
9 Nov 2026CNBC ↗
New Flavor

Koikeya Brings Back Yumeikoro Chips With Rock Salt and Onion Consommé

Koikeya is again turning Hokkaido’s Yumeikoro potato, a Kitami-bred successor to Danshaku certified as a Hokkaido superior variety, into limited chips. Rock Salt and Onion Consommé (Hokkaido onions) go on sale at noon on November 5 only through the Koikeya online shop, in 70 g six-packs at ¥1,684 and a tasting set at ¥3,198, capped at about 10,000 sets after last year’s sell-out.

Who We Are

About World of Chips

We’re on a mission to document every potato chip flavor, brand, and snacking tradition on Earth. From Japan’s seasonal Calbee limited editions to South Africa’s beloved Simba Chutney chips, we believe every crisp tells a story about the culture it comes from.

World of Chips is an independent project born out of a genuine love for potato chips (the thin, crispy, bagged kind — not fries!). We research global markets, track new flavor launches, and build tools to help chip enthusiasts explore snack culture worldwide.
